<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/build/first-run/ -->

# Driver setup and first run

A gripper from the shop arrives with its driver configured: the stepper calibrated, gripper mode on, the
thermistor on, the gains set, everything saved. A gripper you build has a bare STEPFOC driver that must be
brought to the same state once, over its UART port. This page is that procedure; the commands are the driver's,
and the [STEPFOC documentation](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/) explains each in depth.

## What you need

- The driver mounted on the stepper with its encoder magnet, before the pinion is engaged in the racks: the
  motor calibration turns the motor several revolutions in both directions, which the racks cannot follow. Do
  this step with the stepper out of the gripper or with the pinion not yet fitted.
- A 3.3 V [USB-to-serial adapter](https://source-robotics.com/products/usb-to-serial-adapter) on the driver's
  UART connector, a terminal at 256000 baud with CR+LF line endings, and 24 V on the driver's power connector.
  [The serial terminal](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/05-setup/terminal/) on the STEPFOC
  site shows the terminal setup.
- The thermistor from the BOM, soldered to the driver's thermistor connector and fixed to the motor housing
  with thermal cement.

Static electricity damages the driver: touch earthed metal before you handle it, hold it by its edges, and
connect and disconnect its cables with the supply off.

## With Motor GUI

[Motor GUI](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/05-setup/motor-gui/), connected over **UART** through the serial adapter, has a preset per stepper on its
setup page: *MSG 21.5 mm motor*, *MSG 40 mm motor* and *MSG 60 mm motor*. A preset writes the stepper's
resistance, inductance and 50 pole pairs, the current limit, the loop gains, gripper mode, the thermistor and
the CAN ID, then saves; its CAN ID is 6, the PAR6 gripper's, so change it before applying for another robot.
Apply it after the motor calibration of step 1: it does step 2 for you.

## 1. The motor calibration

Restore the defaults first, so that nothing from another motor or junk in the EEPROM goes into the calibration,
then enter the stepper's parameters and calibrate:

| Stepper | `#PP` | `#R` | `#L` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21.5 mm, 17HS08-1004S | 50 | 3.7 | 0.0045 |
| 40 mm, 17HS16-2004S1 | 50 | 1.1 | 0.0026 |
| 60 mm, 17HS24-2104S | 50 | 1.6 | 0.0030 |

```
#Default
#PP 50
#R 1.1
#L 0.0026
#Cal
```

The motor turns, the driver prints each step and ends with `Calibration success!`. The whole routine and its
messages are in [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/05-setup/calibration/) on
the STEPFOC site. `#Default` also resets the serial number the driver reports; note what `#SERNUM` prints before
you start if you need it.

!!! note "STEPFOC firmware 109 and newer"
    From STEPFOC firmware 109 a successful `#Cal` is followed by two runs of its own, the encoder table and the
    anti-cogging: the motor turns slowly for about another minute, and the driver saves everything when they
    finish. Keep the pinion off until then, and start step 2 when `#Info` no longer shows `running:` under
    `In force:`. The encoder-table run holds 80 % of the current limit in the coils for some 20 s; after
    `#Default` the limit is 1700 mA, so set `#Ilim` for the stepper (its maximum in
    [Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/)) before `#Cal`. See
    [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/05-setup/calibration/) on the STEPFOC
    site.

!!! success "Check"
    The terminal ends with `Calibration success!`, and `#Info` prints `Calibrated`, `Number of pole pairs: 50` and
    the resistance and inductance you entered. If it ends with `Calibration failed!`, the STEPFOC page
    [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/05-setup/calibration/) explains each message.

## 2. The gripper settings

```
#Gripper 1
#Term 1
#Tlim 75
#Kpiq 1.4047
#Kiiq 0.1149
#CANID 0
#Save
```

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `#Gripper 1` | gripper mode: the driver runs the gripper state machine and answers the gripper messages |
| `#Term 1`, `#Tlim 75` | the thermistor on, the temperature limit at 75 °C. Without it the motor can burn out under a long grip |
| `#Kpiq 1.4047`, `#Kiiq 0.1149` | the current loop gains of Motor GUI's gripper presets on firmware 108 and older, the same for the three steppers. From 109 the presets send `#Cbw 160` and each stepper's own gains (21.5 mm 4.828 / 0.5951, 40 mm 2.7033 / 0.1769, 60 mm 3.1464 / 0.2574), `#Kpv 0.014` / `#Kiv 0.00014` for the 21.5 mm and 0.02 / 0.001 for the others, and the tool id, `#Tool` 11 to 33 (tens: the rail, 1 = 100, 2 = 150, 3 = 200 mm; units: the stepper, 1 = 21.5, 2 = 40, 3 = 60 mm). On 108 the gains the calibration computes for the stepper are sharper than a gripper needs |
| `#CANID 0` | the node ID on the robot's bus; 0 to 13, see [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/can/) |
| `#Save` | nothing above survives a power cycle until it is saved |

!!! success "Check"
    After a power cycle, `#Info` prints `CAN ID is: 0` and `Gripper: 1`, and `#Gripinfo` prints `I am a gripper`.
    If not, the settings were not saved: enter them again and end with `#Save`.

## 3. Assemble and calibrate the gripper

Fit the pinion and assemble the gripper, power it up, and run the gripper calibration (`#Gripcal`, or Motor GUI's
**Calibrate**): the jaws open fully and close fully. Then a first move at a low current, as in
[Calibrate, activate, move](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/05-setup/first-moves/). `#Gripinfo` prints the gripper's state, including the end stops the
calibration found.

!!! success "Check"
    The jaws opened fully and closed fully, `#Gripinfo` prints `Gripper calibrated is: 1`, and a move at a low
    current goes to its position. If the calibration gives up after 24 s:
    [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/09-troubleshooting/#calibration).

## Current limit

The gripper's moves use the current limit of each command, not the driver's `#Ilim`. Keep the commanded current
at or below the stepper's maximum current ([Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/)); the
firmware clamps it only at 2800 mA.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/appendix/performance/ -->

# Performance tests

A thermal test of the MSG gripper. The thermal limit is 75 °C at the thermistor on the motor housing.

!!! warning
    A gripper built without the thermistor on its motor has no temperature protection and can damage its motor
    in normal operation.

## Several days of cycling

- Open and close every 2.5 s, no load: the current near 0
- 7 days without interruption
- Motor temperature: 42 °C
- Ambient temperature: 33 °C


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/appendix/firmware-release-notes/ -->

# Firmware release notes

What changed in each release of the STEPFOC firmware the gripper runs, from the release notes in the driver's
repository, up to the release this site describes. Entries about the driver's motion modes do not concern a
gripper; the gripper mode, the CAN protocol and the bootloader do.

## V109 (2026-11-10)

STEPFOC firmware **V109** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader. From 109 the STEPFOC and the Spectral Micro share their version numbers. Everything below is described in the manual: [STEPFOC docs](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/); what a driver keeps and what to run after the update: [Upgrading from older firmware](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/07-firmware/upgrading/).

#### New features
- **Parameters:** any setting or read-out by number over CAN (commands 36-38) or `#Par`: the gains and limits, the watchdog, the current loop, the speed estimate, the tool id and more (parameters 1-87). Identity (39) and telemetry (40) frames.
- **Capture, histogram and buffers** (41-43): record three signals from the control loop, read the encoder and anti-cogging tables.
- **Watchdog actions:** on a lost host the driver can idle, brake, coast, hold the position, or descend at a capped speed, with a fallback time.
- **Current loop from R, L and one bandwidth** (parameter 49, default 160 Hz); the direct PLL speed estimate at 60 Hz by default; commutation delay compensation, 166 µs by default; a position input filter and a velocity-integral deadband.
- **Encoder table and anti-cogging measured on the driver:** `#Cal` runs the calibration, then the encoder table and the anti-cogging identification, and saves; `#Calonly` is the calibration alone.
- **Sound through the motor:** tones, a queue of notes and samples (CAN 44 and 45, `#Tone`).
- **Identification:** `#Info` and parameters 84-87 report the build (git commit), the board ID and a calibration ID.
- **Settings in blocks with their own checksums;** a reset keeps the CAN ID; a product lock refuses a Spectral image on a STEPFOC board.

#### Calibration
- The angle alignment locks the rotor with the calibration current through the coil's resistance (it used a fixed 0.5 V, too weak for small motors with a high coil resistance). On a 20 mm stepper the alignment offset now comes out 6× steadier from run to run; 25 of 25 calibrations passed.
- Kt and KV are measured in four spins alternating direction at a forced 6 V; a warning only when two same-direction spins differ by more than 5 %.
- `#Cal` from a moving motor switches the bridge off first; a failed calibration switches it off at once; an E-stop ends a calibration, and `#Cal` is refused while one is latched (`Cal: not started, the E-stop is latched (#Clear first)`); the alignment starts from its first stage after a calibration that was ended from outside. `#Calangle` is refused while the driver is in error.
- The current limit is put back when a calibration ends.

#### Safety
- Limits: a negative or not-a-number value is ignored by the legacy CAN frames (limits, gains, Kt, voltage limit 0-60000 mV); `#Ilim` and `#Vlimit` take the magnitude; the current of a gripper move stays within 0-2800 mA; `#PP` takes 1-200 pole pairs, only while idle. PWM duties stay between 0 and 100 %.
- The current-sense zero waits for the motor supply: started on USB before the supply, the driver used a zero about 100 mA off. It now says so in `#Info` and measures the zero by itself once the supply is there.
- No undervoltage error while the supply ramps up at power-up.

#### CAN bus
- A gripper poll right after a new move command no longer cancels it as new: object detection reports contact again (it read "at position" while pressing on an object). The same in every release before 109.
- The current and PD frames set their setpoint and mode together. Length codes above 8 are read as 8; extended (29-bit) frames are ignored.
- Watchdog: setting its time or a save starts a fresh window; a negative time means off; hold and descend no longer use the last moving loop's delay compensation.

#### Bug fixes
- After `#Cal`, a host that takes the driver within 3 s drops the encoder-table and anti-cogging runs (they used to start by themselves at the next idle). `#Encal` and `#Cogcal` start only on their own words. While such a run turns the motor, a capture is not armed and the histogram is not changed.
- A storage block whose check fails is read up to three times before its defaults are used. `#Info` says the anti-cogging is saved only while what is in RAM equals what is stored.
- The current-loop integrals are cleared whenever the bridge brakes or coasts. The sound queue and sample buffer no longer replay old content after a stop; a pitch the driver cannot play answers `Tone: not played`.

#### Compatibility
- Python library **1.21 or newer** (`pip install --upgrade Spectral-BLDC`), Motor GUI **0.5.0**.
- The calibration and the settings of 108 are kept. Not tested on the bench for this release: an upgrade from V103 with the ST-Link, and a downgrade.

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V109.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `94bc56430195b323f48dd47237be99700623ec8d0ae391f974a809e3eae123cc`
- Size: 112088 bytes

Built from commit 118fe17 on `bootloader-version` (`#Info` shows it as `Build: 118FE17`). Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V108 (2026-08-26)

STEPFOC firmware **V108** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### Bug fixes
- Fixed calibration (`#Cal`) spuriously failing with `Phase order is wrong!` on otherwise-healthy motors. The "confirm commutation" pre-check (before the real angle-offset search) commands a pure torque-axis voltage using the not-yet-calibrated encoder angle — depending on a given unit's actual rotor-to-encoder mounting angle, that command could land almost entirely on the wrong axis and produce ~zero torque, failing the check even though nothing was actually broken. Bench-confirmed on a real unit.
- Fix: retry the pre-check once at a 90° angle bias before declaring failure — guaranteed to land within 45° of the true torque axis on at least one of the two tries. The downstream angle-offset search is unaffected and already independent of this pre-check.
- Added `Spin-confirm delta` / `Vbus` diagnostics to `#Cal`'s failure report, for the rare case both tries still fail.

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V108.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `25cbc4887ca2c192eba6e708930eb6b6c677fd1e76299313c3b3ce3459e0e8a1`
- Size: 99188 bytes

Built from commit 46b4911 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V107 (2026-08-24)

STEPFOC firmware **V107** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### Bug fixes
- Fixed PD mode (`IN_DATA_PACK_PD` over CAN): the commanded speed was written into `Feedforward_speed`, but `PD_mode()` reads `Velocity_setpoint` for its KD term — so the KD (velocity-damping) term of the impedance controller was always evaluated against a stale/zero setpoint and had no effect. The CAN handler now writes the field the control law actually reads. `IN_DATA_PACK_1` / position mode is unaffected — `Feedforward_speed` there is correct and continues to feed the position cascade.

#### CAN bus
- Added a generic settings command (`IN_SETTINGS`) so future boolean settings don't each need their own command ID. Payload is `mask` + `value` (one byte each), one bit per setting — only bits set in the mask are applied, so a sender only needs to know about the bits it cares about.
- First setting on this command: brake vs. coast (bit 0), previously only selectable over UART (`Brake` / `Coast`), now selectable over CAN as well.

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V107.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `63699037c79318e1d78738edcb13e9f9bc00a3393dc5803f920b244a60622ae2`
- Size: 98972 bytes

Built from commit 04ec180 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V106 (2026-07-05)

STEPFOC firmware **V106** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### CAN bus
- The controller now drains up to 8 CAN messages per pass instead of just 1, so short bursts (multiple commands sent back-to-back, or a busy multi-node bus) no longer silently drop messages once the 3-deep hardware FIFO fills.
- A CAN peripheral that fails to initialize no longer bricks the board — UART stays fully usable, only the CAN bus is skipped.

#### Safety
- Added a hardware watchdog (100ms). If the control loop ever stops running, the board resets instead of leaving the motor driven at a stale duty cycle.
- Fixed a bug where `Torque_mode` could silently overwrite your commanded Iq setpoint when clamping to the current limit — reading it back after clamping now shows what you actually asked for, and raising the current limit afterward immediately restores the original commanded torque instead of requiring the command to be resent.
- Fixed undefined behavior in a serial-protocol integer conversion (`fourBytesToInt`).
- Synced default configuration values that had drifted between two locations in the code, so a fresh `#Default` and a freshly-flashed board's built-in defaults now agree.

#### EEPROM / configuration integrity
- Added CRC validation over the saved configuration, split into two independent halves: **calibration data** (resistance, inductance, Kt/KV, angle offset, current-loop gains, etc.) and **settings** (PID tuning, limits, watchdog config, CAN ID, etc.).
- This means a corrupted save (e.g. from a power loss mid-write) is detected and safely defaulted instead of silently running with garbage values — and critically, a *future* firmware update that only adds a new setting can no longer wipe your calibration, since the two are validated independently.
- Boards upgrading from older, pre-CRC firmware keep their existing calibration automatically — no need to recalibrate after this update.
- A few unused slots were reserved in the calibration block for upcoming features (e.g. magnet alignment), so those can be added later without another migration.

#### Performance
- PWM output no longer re-resolves which timer/channel it's writing to on every single call (it was doing this 4x per control tick) — resolved once and cached, freeing up ISR headroom.
- Velocity calculation switched from a floating-point divide to an integer multiply.

#### Usability
- New `#Help` command — prints a summary of the available commands.
- Serial now responds with "Unknown command" for unrecognized input instead of silently ignoring it.
- Calibration now prints progress during the angle-offset search (previously up to ~40 seconds of silence that could look like the board had hung).
- `#Error` now also reports driver faults (undervoltage/thermal/overcurrent), not just the other error types.
- `#Info` now always reports live ISR execution time, useful for checking control-loop headroom on the bench.

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V106.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `bc061fb273e7c836e3180fa597ecd373e7e357b0eab9130b63a7fd19b70a6073`
- Size: 98940 bytes

Built from commit 661e7d3 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V105 (2026-07-04)

STEPFOC firmware **V105** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### What's new
- Reversed stepper phase wiring now calibrates automatically — no more "switch phases and try again." The firmware detects the wiring and compensates it in software, so **all 8 phase-wiring permutations calibrate identically and symmetrically**.
- `#Info` now reports the firmware's own build version, so the version is correct immediately after flashing (no `#Default` needed).

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V105.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `0d80ce3cf78109f6ff54697425ed475ffca4e97e220d72fe0823ce1bd60a4908`
- Size: 95924 bytes

Built from commit bda57d6 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V103 (2025-12-28)

First stable release for public

## V102 (2025-12-28)

First official release for the public

## V101 (2025-09-29)

Initial fully functional release based on spectral micro firmware.

# Versions and compatibility

Which STEPFOC firmware release works with which bootloader, gripper hardware, Python library and ROS 2 driver.
One row per firmware release, newest first; the last column names the version of this site, a gripper release, that
describes it.

| Firmware (STEPFOC) | Released | Bootloader | MSG gripper | Python library (Spectral-BLDC) | ROS 2 driver | Docs (gripper release) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 109 | 2026-11-10 | required | V1.2, V1.1 | 1.21 or newer (1.20 swaps object detection 1 and 2) | msg_gripper_ros2 (ROS 2 Humble) | 1.2 |
| 108 | 2026-08-26 | required (installed on grippers shipped with 104 or newer) | V1.2, V1.1 | 1.20 or newer | msg_gripper_ros2 (ROS 2 Humble) | 1.2 |
| 107 | 2026-08-24 | required | V1.1 | 1.20 or newer | msg_gripper_ros2 | not published |
| 106 | 2026-07-05 | required | V1.1 | 1.19 or newer | msg_gripper_ros2 | not published |
| 105 | 2026-07-04 | required (the first release that needs it) | V1.1 | 1.19 or newer | msg_gripper_ros2 | not published |
| 103 | 2025-12-28 | none (flashed with a programming adapter) | V1.1 | 1.17 or newer | msg_gripper_ros2 | the STEPFOC site, version 103 |

Send_Respond_Device_Info returns the firmware release a gripper runs; `#Info` prints it over UART.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/terminology/ -->

# Glossary

**Action bit**
:   A bit of the move command: 1 carries out the move, 0 stops the move and holds the jaws still, with the
    command stored. The action status of the answer repeats this bit.

**Activated**
:   A flag the gripper keeps, set by the activate bit of the move command or by `#Gripact`. A move is carried out
    only while the gripper is activated and calibrated.

**CAN ID** (node ID)
:   The address of the gripper on the CAN bus, 0 to 13; every gripper ships as 0. It occupies bits 10 to 7 of the
    11-bit CAN frame identifier; the command ID occupies bits 6 to 1 and the error bit is bit 0.

**CANvas**
:   Source Robotics' USB-to-CAN adapter. It appears as a serial port and speaks slcan, which `python-can`, Motor
    GUI and the ROS 2 driver use.

**Current limit** (grip force)
:   The current, in mA, the driver may put into the motor during a move. Torque is current times the motor's
    torque constant, so the current limit sets the force with which the jaws press on an object.

**Driver**
:   The STEPFOC board on the back of the gripper's stepper: field-oriented control of the motor, the gripper state
    machine and the CAN and UART interfaces. The gripper's firmware is the driver's firmware.

**E-stop bit**
:   A bit of the move command. 1 stops the gripper and raises the gripper E-stop error, which comes back at every
    cycle while the last command's bit is 1: send a command with the bit at 0, then clear the error.

**Error bit**
:   Bit 0 of every CAN frame identifier the driver sends: 1 while any error is active.

**Field-oriented control** (FOC)
:   Controlling the stepper's current as a vector relative to the rotor, from the driver's encoder. It turns the
    stepper into a motor whose torque is known and limited, which is what makes a force-controlled gripper out
    of it.

**Firmware release**
:   One build of the STEPFOC firmware, numbered 103, 104, 105, … and tagged `V103`, `V104`, … in the driver's
    repository. `#Info` prints the release a gripper runs. This documentation describes one release; the version
    selector switches between them.

**Gripper calibration**
:   The routine (`Send_gripper_calibrate`, `#Gripcal`) that opens the jaws fully, then closes them fully, at low
    force, and records both end stops as positions 0 and 255. Needed after every power-up.

**Gripper mode**
:   The driver's mode in which it runs a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved): move commands with a jaw position, a speed
    and a current limit, and object detection.

**Motor calibration**
:   The driver's own calibration of the stepper (`#Cal`): the pole pairs, resistance and inductance entered, the
    encoder aligned, the motor constants measured. Done once, at the factory or when you build the gripper; not
    to be confused with the gripper calibration.

**Object detection**
:   The gripper's report of why the jaws stopped: 0 still moving, 1 an object stopped them while closing, 2 an
    object stopped them while opening, 3 they reached the commanded position.

**Position**
:   The jaw position as the gripper commands and reports it: 0 fully open, 255 fully closed, linear in between.

**Rack and pinion**
:   The gripper's mechanism: a pinion on the motor shaft meshes with two racks that run on the linear rail in
    opposite directions, so one motor moves both jaws symmetrically.

**Speed**
:   The speed of a move, 0 to 255, mapped by the firmware to 500 to 60000 encoder ticks per second of the motor.

**Stroke**
:   How much the distance between the jaw carriers changes from fully open to fully closed: 55, 105 or 155 mm,
    set by the rail length. Each jaw travels half of it.

**Timeout error** (watchdog)
:   The driver's CAN watchdog, as the gripper reports it: when the watchdog is set (`Send_Watchdog`) and no
    gripper command or status request arrives in time, the gripper stops and raises it.

**Watchdog**
:   A timer the driver resets with every gripper command (full or empty) and every status request it receives.
    When it is set and runs out, the gripper reports a timeout error and stops.

# API reference

The gripper's CAN messages and UART commands, its status and error bits, and the Python library calls that send
them, for the firmware named on the landing page. The gripper is a STEPFOC stepper driver in gripper mode and accepts the
driver's whole command set; only what a gripper host or a self-built gripper needs is here, the rest is in the
[STEPFOC reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/reference/).

- [CAN messages](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/): the identifier, and the gripper, system and status messages
- [UART commands](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/): the gripper commands, the driver setup commands, status and utility
- [Errors and status bits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/errors/)
- [Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/python/): which library call sends which message

**Conventions.** Bytes are numbered from 0 and multi-byte values are big-endian. Bits are numbered from the most
significant: bit 7 is the first flag in a byte. The position is 0 (open) to 255 (closed), the speed 0 to 255, the
current in mA. UART command names are case-sensitive.

The command IDs, frame lengths and responses are read from the firmware's source at its release tag when the site
is built, so they cannot drift from the firmware; the descriptions and byte layouts are written by hand.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can-tools/ -->

# CAN frame tool and downloads

Build or inspect a frame using the command definitions of this manual's firmware release. All calculations
run in your browser; the tool does not connect to an adapter or send commands to hardware.

## Downloads

[Command definitions (JSON)](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/assets/can/protocol-V109.json) · [Gripper DBC](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/assets/can/protocol-V109-gripper.dbc)

The JSON includes the firmware tag, source commit, message IDs, every documented layout and its bit order.
The DBC files cover **nodes 0 to 13**, with both the clean and fault-bit identifiers of driver replies.
Reserved commands are omitted. Values use the firmware's native units: ticks, ticks/s, mA and the units in
the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/).

An RTR request uses the same identifier as its data reply. DBC describes the **data reply**; it does not
represent the request's RTR flag or the empty gripper status poll. Both are supported by the browser tool.

The gripper's two object-detection bits have an unusual order: bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit.
The DBC signal `gripper_object_detection_raw` retains the wire value and supplies text labels (raw 2 =
object while closing, raw 1 = object while opening). The browser decoder converts that pair to the firmware's
numeric status (1 = closing, 2 = opening).

## Try a frame

The example `0x07A`, data `C8 1E 01 2C C0`, is a command to gripper node 0: position 200, speed 30,
current 300 mA, activate and action set, E-stop and release direction clear. These are an illustration of the
encoding; the device's current and motion limits still apply. Select another message above the fields to build
one of its documented forms. To inspect a reply, enter its identifier and data bytes below.

<div class="can-tool" data-schema="../../assets/can/protocol-V109.json" markdown="0">
  <p class="can-tool__status" role="status">Loading the firmware's command definitions…</p>
  <fieldset><legend>Build a frame</legend>
    <label for="ct-node">Node ID (0–13)</label><input id="ct-node" name="node" type="number" min="0" max="13" step="1" value="0">
    <label for="ct-command">Message and layout</label><select id="ct-command" name="command"></select>
    <label><input name="error" type="checkbox"> Driver reply has an active fault (error bit 1)</label>
    <div class="can-tool__fields"></div>
    <button type="button" name="build" class="md-button md-button--primary">Build frame</button>
    <pre class="can-tool__built" aria-live="polite"></pre>
    <button type="button" name="use" class="md-button">Use this frame in the decoder</button>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset><legend>Decode a frame</legend>
    <label for="ct-id">CAN identifier (hex)</label><input id="ct-id" name="identifier" type="text" value="0x07A" spellcheck="false">
    <label for="ct-data">Data bytes (hex, up to eight)</label><input id="ct-data" name="data" type="text" value="C8 1E 01 2C C0" spellcheck="false">
    <label><input name="remote" type="checkbox"> Remote request (RTR; no payload)</label>
    <button type="button" name="decode" class="md-button md-button--primary">Decode frame</button>
    <div class="can-tool__decoded" aria-live="polite"></div>
  </fieldset>
  <noscript>Enable JavaScript for the frame tool, or use the reference tables and downloads above.</noscript>
</div>

**Check:** the example decodes to the values above. Change the identifier to `0x1FA` to see the same command
addressed to node 3. An invalid length or out-of-range field produces an explanation instead of a frame.

For wiring, termination, host timing and recovery, use [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/can/). To look up a
message's purpose and accepted lengths, use the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/ -->

# CAN messages

CAN 2.0, 1 Mbit/s, 11-bit identifiers. The identifier carries the node ID (bits 10 to 7, 0 to 13), the command ID
(bits 6 to 1, 0 to 63) and, in frames from the gripper, the error bit (bit 0). [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/can/)
explains how the pieces are used; this page lists them.

Three kinds of message:

- **Send_…** — the host sends data to the gripper. The gripper command is answered with Respond_Gripper_data_pack;
  the others are not answered.
- **Send_Respond_…** — the host asks for data with a **remote frame** (RTR bit set, no data) under the command ID;
  the gripper answers with a data frame under the same command ID.
- **Respond_…** — frames only the gripper sends.

Multi-byte values are big-endian (data[0] first); bits inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit
(bit 7 first).

## The messages a gripper needs

| ID | Message | Direction | Length | Group |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [Send_ESTOP](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_estop) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 1 | [Send_Clear_Error](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 9 | [Respond_Heartbeat](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#respond_heartbeat) | driver → host | 0 | Status requests |
| 10 | [Send_Respond_Ping](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_ping) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 0 | Status requests |
| 11 | [Send_CAN_ID](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_can_id) | host → driver | 1 | System |
| 12 | [Send_Idle](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_idle) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 13 | [Send_Save_config](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_save_config) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 14 | [Send_Reset](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_reset) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 15 | [Send_Watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) | host → driver | 5 | System |
| 23 | [Send_Respond_Temperature](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_temperature) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 2 | Status requests |
| 24 | [Send_Respond_Voltage](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_voltage) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 2 | Status requests |
| 25 | [Send_Respond_Device_Info](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_device_info) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 7 | Status requests |
| 26 | [Send_Respond_State_of_Errors](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_state_of_errors) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 2 | Status requests |
| 30 | [Send_Heartbeat_Setup](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_heartbeat_setup) | host → driver | 4 | System |
| 60 | [Respond_Gripper_data_pack](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/gripper/#respond_gripper_data_pack) | driver → host | 4 | Gripper |
| 61 | [Send_gripper_data_pack](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_data_pack) | host → driver | 0, 5 | Gripper |
| 62 | [Send_gripper_calibrate](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_calibrate) | host → driver | 0 | Gripper |

The driver's other messages (the motion commands, the gains and limits, the encoder and current requests) are
not listed here; they are in the [STEPFOC CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/reference/can/).

## By group

- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/gripper/): the move command and its answer, the gripper calibration
- [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/): node ID, E-stop, idle, save, reset, clear, watchdog, heartbeat setup
- [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/): temperature, voltage, identity, the driver's error flags, the heartbeat

## The Python library

Every message the host can send has a method of the same name in `Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN`, listed in
[Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/python/).

## Tools and downloads

[Build or decode a CAN frame, and download this firmware's JSON and DBC definitions](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can-tools/).

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

The move command, its answer, and the gripper calibration. [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/how-it-works/)
explains what the gripper does with them.

### Send_gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 61</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 or 5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_data_pack()`</span></div>

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state. The answer is sent before the driver acts on the frame, so it carries the state from before it. While the gripper calibration runs, send only the empty frame: a full one ends the calibration.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1 |  | Speed | unsigned 8-bit | 0 slowest, 255 fastest |
| 2-3 |  | Current | signed 16-bit | current limit of the move in mA, the grip force; clamped by the firmware only at 2800 mA, keep it at or below the stepper's rated current (Force and speed) |
| 4 | 7 | Activate | bit | 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate |
| 4 | 6 | Action | bit | 1 go to the position, 0 stop and hold the jaws still |
| 4 | 5 | E-stop | bit | 1 raises the gripper E-stop error, again at every cycle while the last command's bit is 1 |
| 4 | 4 | Release direction | bit | read by the firmware but not used |

The driver answers with **Respond_Gripper_data_pack**.

---

### Respond_Gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 60</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated`.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | gripper_position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1-2 |  | gripper_current | signed 16-bit | measured current in mA |
| 3 | 7 | gripper_activated | bit | 1 activated |
| 3 | 6 | gripper_action_status | bit | the action bit of the last command, as received; stays 1 while holding, not changed by the calibration |
| 3 | 5-4 | gripper_object_detection | 2 bits | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | 3 | gripper_temperature_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 2 | gripper_timeout_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 1 | gripper_estop_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 0 | gripper_calibrated | bit | 1 calibrated |

---

### Send_gripper_calibrate

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 62</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_calibrate()`</span></div>

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up. It has no answer: poll with empty Send_gripper_data_pack frames until the calibrated bit is 1, and send nothing else meanwhile, since a full gripper command or Send_Clear_Error ends the calibration. With an error active the request is dropped: clear first.

The driver does not answer this command.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/ -->

# System

Node ID, stopping, saving, resetting, clearing errors, the watchdog and the heartbeat setup: the driver's system
messages a gripper host uses.

### Send_CAN_ID

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 11</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_CAN_ID()`</span></div>

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). The driver answers to the new ID at once; Send_Save_config keeps it over a power cycle and also writes it into the bootloader's board ID.

**1 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | ID | unsigned 8-bit | 0 to 15 |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_ESTOP

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 0</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_ESTOP()`</span></div>

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Idle

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 12</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Idle()`</span></div>

Puts the driver in idle mode (the motor coasts or brakes, see Send_Settings).

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Save_config

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 13</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Save_config()`</span></div>

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Reset

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 14</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Reset()`</span></div>

Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Clear_Error

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 1</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Clear_Error()`</span></div>

Clears the error flags and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; the gripper's E-stop error comes back while the last gripper command's E-stop bit is 1, so send a command with the bit at 0 first. A clear also ends a running gripper calibration. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Watchdog

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 15</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Watchdog()`</span></div>

Sets the watchdog: the gripper command (full or empty) and the status requests reset it, Send_Clear_Error, Send_gripper_calibrate and the setup messages do not; when the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and stops. 0 turns it off (the default). The action byte is stored but not acted on by this firmware: the driver always stops into its idle behaviour.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Time | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |
| 4 |  | Action | unsigned 8-bit | 0 idle, 1 hold, 2 brake (stored only) |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Heartbeat_Setup

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 30</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()`</span></div>

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Interval | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/ -->

# Status requests

Remote frames the host sends under a command ID, answered by the gripper with a data frame under the same ID,
and the heartbeat the gripper sends on its own when it is set up.

### Send_Respond_Ping

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 10</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Ping()`</span></div>

Asks the driver to answer with an empty frame, to see that it is on the bus.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Ping**.

---

### Send_Respond_Temperature

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 23</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Temperature()`</span></div>

Asks for the thermistor temperature. Meaningful only with the thermistor enabled (`#Term 1`).

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | temperature | signed 16-bit | °C |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Temperature**.

---

### Send_Respond_Voltage

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 24</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Voltage()`</span></div>

Asks for the supply voltage.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | voltage | unsigned 16-bit | mV |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Voltage**.

---

### Send_Respond_Device_Info

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 25</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Device_Info()`</span></div>

Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version, batch date and serial number from the EEPROM, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM).

**The frame** (7 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | HARDWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | PCB revision |
| 1 |  | BATCH_DATE | unsigned 8-bit | production batch |
| 2 |  | SOFTWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | firmware release, e.g. 108 |
| 3-6 |  | SERIAL_NUMBER | unsigned 32-bit | serial number |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Device_Info**.

---

### Send_Respond_State_of_Errors

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 26</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()`</span></div>

Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated and watchdog states.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 7 | error | bit | any error is active |
| 0 | 6 | temperature_error | bit | motor over the temperature limit |
| 0 | 5 | encoder_error | bit | magnet not detected or misaligned |
| 0 | 4 | vbus_error | bit | supply voltage outside the limits |
| 0 | 3 | driver_error | bit | the MOSFET driver reports undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent |
| 0 | 2 | velocity_error | bit | speed over the limit |
| 0 | 1 | current_error | bit | reserved; never set by this firmware |
| 0 | 0 | estop_error | bit | Send_ESTOP was received |
| 1 | 7 | calibrated | bit | the motor is calibrated |
| 1 | 6 | activated | bit | the controller is activated |
| 1 | 5 | watchdog_error | bit | the watchdog ran out |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_State_of_Errors**.

---

### Respond_Heartbeat

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 9</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span></div>

The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/ -->

# UART commands

The commands a gripper needs over the driver's serial port, for the firmware release this site describes. The
kind, the argument type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the
descriptions are written by hand. [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/uart/) says where the port is and how it is
used.

## Syntax

```
#<Name> [number]
```

- A **Set/Get** command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
- A **Get** command only prints.
- An **Action** command does something; a number after it is ignored.
- Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the number at most 19; the line ends with LF (CR before it is
  fine). 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
- A name the parser does not know is answered `Unknown command`.

## The commands a gripper needs

| Command | Kind | Argument | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`#Cal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Calibrated`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#CANID`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#Cbw`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Clear`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Default`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Action |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Error`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Gripact`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Action |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcur`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripinfo`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Get |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripper`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Grippos`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripstop`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripvel`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Help`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Ilim`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#Info`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Kiiq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Kpiq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Kt`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#L`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#LED`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Magnet`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Mode`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#PP`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#R`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Reset`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Save`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/) | Action |  | Driver setup |

| [`#Vbus`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |

The driver's other commands (motion, gains, the calibration settings) are in the
[STEPFOC UART reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/reference/uart/).

## By group

- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/): gripper mode, the gripper calibration, the setpoints, the state
- [Driver setup](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/): the defaults, the motor parameters and calibration, the gains, the thermistor, the node ID, saving
- [Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/): identity, errors, temperature, help

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Gripper` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Whether this driver is a gripper. A gripper has it set and saved; `#Default` clears it, so set it again after restoring the defaults. | the flag |
| `#Gripcal` | Action |  | Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Clear any error first; until `#Gripinfo` reports it calibrated, send no `#Grippos` or `#Clear`, which end it. Enters **gripper calibration** mode. | `Gripper calibration!` |
| `#Gripinfo` | Get |  | Prints the gripper state: gripper mode, calibrated, activated, the position, speed and current setpoints, the E-stop and action bits, the object detection, and the end stops in encoder ticks. | the report |
| `#Gripstop` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The gripper E-stop bit. While it is 1, the E-stop error is raised again at every cycle: set it to 0 before `#Clear`. | the bit |
| `#Gripact` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The activate bit. | the bit |
| `#Gripcur` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The current limit of gripper moves, the grip force. The firmware clamps it only at 2800 mA; keep it at or below the stepper's rated current (see Force and speed). | the setpoint |
| `#Gripvel` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 255 | The speed setpoint of gripper moves. | the setpoint |
| `#Grippos` | Set/Get | int: 0 (open) to 255 (closed) | The position setpoint; also activates the gripper, sets the action bit and goes to gripper mode. Enters **gripper** mode. | the current position |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/setup/ -->

# Driver setup

The driver commands a self-built gripper is configured with; [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/build/first-run/)
is the procedure.

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Kpiq` | Set/Get | gain | Kp of the Iq current loop; also sets Kpid. | the current value |
| `#Kiiq` | Set/Get | gain | Ki of the Iq current loop; also sets Kiid. | the current value |
| `#R` | Set/Get | resistance in Ω | The phase resistance of the motor (one coil). STEPFOC does not measure it; enter the datasheet value before Cal. | the current value |
| `#L` | Set/Get | inductance in H | The phase inductance of the motor (one coil); enter the datasheet value before Cal. | the current value |
| `#Kt` | Set/Get | Nm/A | The torque constant, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#Cal` | Get |  | Runs the driver's motor calibration (see Driver configuration): enter PP, R and L first, with the pinion not yet in the rack. | the calibration log |
| `#Cal` | Get |  | Runs the driver's motor calibration (see Driver configuration): enter PP, R and L first, with the pinion not yet in the rack. | the calibration log |
| `#Save` | Action |  | Writes the configuration to the EEPROM. Do it after calibration and after tuning. | `Save` |
| `#Ilim` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The driver's Iq current limit outside gripper mode; the firmware clamps it to 2800 mA. Gripper moves use Gripcur instead. | the current limit |
| `#Tlim` | Set/Get | int: temperature in °C | The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default. | `Temp limit N` |
| `#Default` | Action |  | Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM, including the serial number, hardware version and batch date, and clears the gripper flag, heartbeat and watchdog. Back those up first. | `Loaded default config!` |
| `#Term` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default). | the setting |
| `#Cbw` | Set/Get | bandwidth in Hz | The current loop bandwidth calibration uses to compute Kpiq and Kiiq. | the bandwidth |
| `#CANID` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 13 | The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Save keeps it over a power cycle and also writes it into the bootloader's board ID. | the ID, or `Invalid CAN ID` |
| `#PP` | Set/Get | int: pole pairs | The motor's pole pairs: 50 for a 1.8° stepper, 75 for 1.2°, 100 for 0.9°, 125 for 0.72°. Calibration accepts only these values. | the current value |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/uart/utility/ -->

# Status and utility

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Magnet` | Get |  | Reads the encoder's magnet status. | `Magnet Good` or `Magnet Bad` |
| `#Reset` | Action |  | Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again. | nothing |
| `#Temp` | Get |  | Prints the thermistor temperature. | °C, or `Temp Off` while the thermistor is disabled |
| `#Mode` | Get |  | Prints the control mode. In gripper mode (mode 11) it prints nothing; `#Gripinfo` shows the gripper's state. | `Idle mode`, `Position control`, `Speed control`, `Current control`, `PD control`, `Open loop`, `Gripper calib mode` during the gripper calibration; `Gripper mode` is what it prints for mode 6, voltage torque |
| `#Vbus` | Get |  | Prints the supply voltage. | mV |
| `#Error` | Get |  | Prints which errors are active. | `No errors!` or `In error state!` followed by one line per active error |
| `#Clear` | Action |  | Clears the errors and goes to idle, and ends a running gripper calibration. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back, the gripper's E-stop too while `#Gripstop` is 1; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or `#Calibrated 1`). Enters **idle** mode. | `Clear errors` |
| `#Help` | Action |  | Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 106. | the reference |
| `#Info` | Action |  | Prints the driver's identity and state: hardware version, batch date and firmware version, the ISR time, the CAN ID, the motor calibration, the thermistor and temperature, the supply voltage and the motor parameters (phase direction and order, pole pairs, R, L, Kt, KV). The serial number is printed by `#SERNUM`, the errors by `#Error`, gripper mode by `#Gripper`. | the report |
| `#Calibrated` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The calibrated flag. `#Calibrated 1` clears a calibration error without calibrating; the motor may still be uncalibrated. | the flag |
| `#LED` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Turns the status LED on or off. | the LED state |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/errors/ -->

# Errors and status bits

## The gripper's state byte

Byte 3 of Respond_Gripper_data_pack, the answer to every gripper command, bits numbered from the most significant:

| Bit | Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `activated` | the activate flag is set |
| 6 | `action_status` | the action bit of the last gripper command, as received (`#Grippos` sets it to 1); it stays 1 while the gripper holds, and the calibration does not change it. The state of a move is in `object_detection` |
| 5, 4 | `object_detection` | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object found while closing, 2 object found while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | `temperature_error` | the thermistor on the motor housing is above the limit |
| 2 | `timeout_error` | the driver's CAN watchdog ran out |
| 1 | `estop_error` | the E-stop bit of a command was received |
| 0 | `calibrated` | the gripper calibration is done |

The Python library's attributes are `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`,
`gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error` and `gripper_calibrated`; library
1.20 and older assemble `gripper_object_detection` with its two bits swapped (1 and 2 exchanged), 1.21 and newer
read them right.

## The driver's error flags

The flags as the firmware keeps them, the line `#Error` prints for each, and where each sits in the two bytes of
Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (bits numbered from the most significant).

| Flag | `#Error` prints | Byte, bit | Raised when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Error` | `In error state!` | 0, 7 | any of the flags below is set (also the error bit of every CAN identifier) |
| `temperature_error` | `Temp error` | 0, 6 | the thermistor reads above `#Tlim` (75 °C) |
| `encoder_error` | `Encoder error` | 0, 5 | the driver's encoder does not see its magnet |
| `Vbus_error` | `Vbus error` | 0, 4 | the supply is below 9 V or above `#Vmax` (29 V after `#Default`) |
| `Driver_error` | `Driver error (undervoltage, thermal shutdown, or overcurrent)` | 0, 3 | the driver stage's fault output is active |
| `Velocity_error` | `Velocity error` | 0, 2 | the motor speed exceeds the driver's limit |
| `Current_error` | `Current error` | 0, 1 | never in this firmware; reserved |
| `ESTOP_error` | `Received ESTOP command` | 0, 0 | Send_ESTOP was received |
| `Calibrated` (0) | `Not calibrated` | 1, 7 (1 = calibrated) | the driver's motor calibration is missing |
| `Activated` | — | 1, 6 | the activated flag, not an error |
| `Watchdog_error` | `Watchdog error` | 1, 5 | the watchdog time passed without a valid CAN frame |

The gripper's `timeout_error` is the driver's `Watchdog_error`; the gripper's `temperature_error` is the driver's.
The gripper's `estop_error` is its own, raised by the E-stop bit of the gripper command, and is distinct from the
driver's `ESTOP_error` raised by Send_ESTOP.

## Clearing

Send_Clear_Error and `#Clear` clear every flag, the gripper's E-stop included, and go to idle; a flag whose cause
persists is set again at once. The gripper's `estop_error` is raised again at every cycle while the E-stop bit of
the last gripper command (or `#Gripstop`) is 1: send a gripper command with the bit at 0 first, then clear. The
driver's `Calibrated` flag is set only by the motor calibration (`#Cal`).

## The LED

The driver's status LED is inside the housing: three short flashes and a pause in normal operation, flashing
every 0.5 s during the motor calibration, on steadily in error mode or while the motor is not calibrated.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/python/ -->

# Python library

The `Spectral-BLDC` package ([Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python),
`pip install Spectral-BLDC`) has one method per CAN message in `Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN`, and
`Spectral_BLDC.CanCommunication` for the bus. [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/python/) shows how they are used
with the gripper.

## Calls and messages

The calls for the messages this reference describes; the library has one for every message of the driver.

| Library call | Sends | Answered with | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Send_gripper_data_pack()` | Send_gripper_data_pack (ID 61) | Respond_Gripper_data_pack | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_data_pack) |
| `Send_gripper_calibrate()` | Send_gripper_calibrate (ID 62) | — | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_calibrate) |
| `Send_CAN_ID()` | Send_CAN_ID (ID 11) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_can_id) |
| `Send_ESTOP()` | Send_ESTOP (ID 0) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_estop) |
| `Send_Idle()` | Send_Idle (ID 12) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_idle) |
| `Send_Save_config()` | Send_Save_config (ID 13) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_save_config) |
| `Send_Reset()` | Send_Reset (ID 14) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_reset) |
| `Send_Clear_Error()` | Send_Clear_Error (ID 1) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) |
| `Send_Watchdog()` | Send_Watchdog (ID 15) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) |
| `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()` | Send_Heartbeat_Setup (ID 30) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/system/#send_heartbeat_setup) |
| `Send_Respond_Ping()` | Send_Respond_Ping (ID 10) | Send_Respond_Ping (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_ping) |
| `Send_Respond_Temperature()` | Send_Respond_Temperature (ID 23) | Send_Respond_Temperature (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_temperature) |
| `Send_Respond_Voltage()` | Send_Respond_Voltage (ID 24) | Send_Respond_Voltage (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_voltage) |
| `Send_Respond_Device_Info()` | Send_Respond_Device_Info (ID 25) | Send_Respond_Device_Info (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_device_info) |
| `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()` | Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (ID 26) | Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_state_of_errors) |

`Send_gripper_data_pack(position, speed, current, activate, action, estop, release_direction)` sends the 5-byte
move; called without arguments it sends the empty frame that only asks for the state.

## Receiving

`CanCommunication.receive_can_messages(timeout)` returns `(message, ids)`: the raw `python-can` message and a tuple
`ids` with `node_id`, `command_id` and `error_bit` from the identifier, or `(None, None)` after the timeout.
`SpectralCAN.UnpackData(message, ids)` decodes the message into the object's attributes:

| Message | Attributes |
|---|---|
| Respond_Gripper_data_pack | `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated` |
| Send_Respond_State_of_Errors | `error`, `temperature_error`, `encoder_error`, `vbus_error`, `driver_error`, `velocity_error`, `current_error`, `estop_error`, `calibrated`, `activated`, `watchdog_error` |
| Send_Respond_Temperature | `temperature` |
| Send_Respond_Voltage | `voltage` |
| Send_Respond_Device_Info | `HARDWARE_VERSION`, `BATCH_DATE`, `SOFTWARE_VERSION`, `SERIAL_NUMBER` |

!!! note "Object detection in the library"
    Library 1.20 and older assemble `gripper_object_detection` with the two bits swapped relative to the
    firmware, so they report 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object detected while opening) and 2 where it sends 1
    (object detected while closing); 0 and 3 are unaffected. 1.21 and newer read them right.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/guides/ -->

# Guides

Worked examples around the gripper.

- [Basic control in Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/guides/basic-control/): the shortest program that calibrates the gripper and opens and
  closes it, from the product repository's README.
- [Teleoperation with two grippers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/guides/teleoperation/): one gripper follows the other and pushes back what it
  feels, over one CAN bus and a few lines of Python.

Building a gripper yourself is in the manual, the [Build guide](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/build/). More examples,
for the driver as much as for the gripper, are in the
[Spectral-BLDC-Python examples](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/tree/main/examples) and in
the [STEPFOC guides](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/guides/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/guides/basic-control/ -->

# Basic control in Python

The shortest program that drives the gripper: it connects through the CANvas adapter, clears the errors,
calibrates, then closes and opens every three seconds and prints what the gripper answers. It is the example from
the product repository's README, with a longer wait for the calibration: the README's 4 s is too short for the
150 and 200 mm rails, and a move command sent while the calibration still runs ends it. `pip install
Spectral-BLDC` is the only requirement. Change `COM20` to your adapter's port (`/dev/ttyACM0` on Linux) and
`node_id` to the gripper's CAN ID if you changed it from 0.

!!! danger
    700 mA closes the jaws with real force, about 14 N with the 21.5 mm stepper and 25 N with the 60 mm. Keep fingers out of the jaws, and start with a lower current
    if the gripper is new to you.

```python
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import time

Communication1 = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM20', bitrate=1000000)
Motor1 = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=Communication1)

Motor1.Send_Clear_Error()
Motor1.Send_gripper_calibrate()
time.sleep(10)                 # the calibration: up to about ten seconds; send nothing meanwhile

temp_var = 0
while True:
   if temp_var == 0:
      Motor1.Send_gripper_data_pack(50,100,700,1,1,0,0)
      temp_var = 1
   elif temp_var == 1:
      Motor1.Send_gripper_data_pack(240,100,700,1,1,0,0)
      temp_var = 0

   message, UnpackedMessageID = Communication1.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.2)

   if message is not None:
      print(f"Message is: {message}")
      print(f"Node ID is : {UnpackedMessageID.node_id}")
      print(f"Message ID is: {UnpackedMessageID.command_id}")
      print(f"Error bit is: {UnpackedMessageID.error_bit}")
      print(f"Timestamp is: {message.timestamp}")

   time.sleep(3)
```

Each answer printed is the one to the command just sent, so it still shows the state from before that move.
The arguments of `Send_gripper_data_pack`, in order: the position (0 open, 255 closed), the speed (0 to 255), the
current limit in mA (the force), then the activate bit, the action bit, the E-stop bit and the release direction.
[With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/python/) explains the library's calls, [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/06-operation/how-it-works/)
the state the gripper answers with, and [Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/) what the
current means in newtons.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.2/guides/teleoperation/ -->

# Teleoperation with two grippers

Two grippers on one CAN bus, coupled so that each follows the other: squeeze one by hand and the other closes;
when the other meets an object, the one in your hand pushes back with the force it feels. A hundred lines of
Python, and the basis of a teleoperation setup with force feedback.

This guide does not use the gripper mode. Both drivers run in **current (torque) mode**, the driver's own motion
command, and the PC closes a position loop between them at a fixed rate. The gripper mode's position, speed and
object detection are not involved; the drivers are plain torque sources here.

## What you need

- Two grippers, calibrated as motors (a bought gripper is), with different node IDs: 0 and 1 (`#CANID 1`,
  `#Save` on one of them over UART).
- Both on one bus with the CANvas adapter, 24 V on both, termination at the two ends.
- `pip install Spectral-BLDC SourceRoboticsToolbox`.

!!! warning
    In current mode the gripper has no end-stop knowledge and no object detection: it pushes with whatever current
    the loop commands. Set the driver's current limit to the stepper's rating (`#Ilim`) on both grippers, start
    with low gains, and keep fingers out of the jaws.

## The idea

Each driver is commanded a current proportional to the difference between the two positions, plus a damping
term on the speed difference and a little damping of its own motion:

$$
I_0 = K_p\,(p_1 - p_0) + K_d\,(v_1 - v_0) - K_k\, v_0, \qquad
I_1 = K_p\,(p_0 - p_1) + K_d\,(v_0 - v_1) - K_k\, v_1
$$

$p$ is the jaw position of each gripper in the same units, $v$ its speed. When the two positions agree, both
currents are zero and the grippers rest. Move one by hand and the difference drives the other after it; block
the other, and the difference drives the one in your hand back with the same current, which is the force you
feel. $K_p$ is the stiffness of the virtual spring between them, $K_d$ its damping.

The two drivers' encoders do not read the same number at the same jaw position, so each position is referred to
a reference reading taken once with both grippers in the same position; the Source Robotics Toolbox's `Joint`
does that bookkeeping and unwraps the encoder over its 16384-tick turns.

## The code

```python
import time
import numpy as np
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import SourceRoboticsToolbox as Toolbox

INTERVAL_S = 0.002                 # the loop rate: 500 Hz
REFERENCE = [10440, 13555]         # each gripper's raw encoder reading with both jaws in the same position

Kp, Kd, Kk = 650, 0.0055, 0.0003   # stiffness, damping between the two, damping of each

bus = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM123', bitrate=1000000)
motors = [Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=i, communication=bus) for i in (0, 1)]
joints = [Toolbox.Joint(encoder_resolution=14, master_position=REFERENCE[i], gear_ratio=1, offset=0, dir=0)
          for i in (0, 1)]

position = np.zeros(2)             # each gripper's position, referred to its reference
sector_known = [False, False]
current = [0, 0]

while True:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for i in (0, 1):               # command the currents; each answer carries position and speed
        motors[i].Send_data_pack_1(Position=None, Speed=None, Current=int(current[i]))
    for _ in (0, 1):
        message, ids = bus.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.001)
        if ids is None:
            continue
        i = ids[0]
        motors[i].UnpackData(message, ids)
        if not sector_known[i]:
            joints[i].determine_sector(motors[i].position)
            sector_known[i] = True
        position[i] = joints[i].get_joint_position(motors[i].position)

    current[0] = Kp * (position[1] - position[0]) + Kd * (motors[1].speed - motors[0].speed) - Kk * motors[0].speed
    current[1] = Kp * (position[0] - position[1]) + Kd * (motors[0].speed - motors[1].speed) - Kk * motors[1].speed

    time.sleep(max(0.0, INTERVAL_S - (time.perf_counter() - t0)))
```

The reference readings: with both grippers powered and their jaws set by hand to the same opening, read each
driver's position as the loop receives it (print `motors[i].position` with both currents at 0) and put the two
numbers in `REFERENCE`.

## Tuning

Start with `Kp` at a tenth of the value above and raise it until the follower tracks the leader without lagging;
raise `Kd` if the pair oscillates. The current the formula produces is in mA and is clamped by each driver's
`#Ilim`, so the stepper's rating is the ceiling of the force feedback. A fixed loop rate matters: a loop that
runs at an uneven rate makes the damping terms noisy.

The full example, with a timer for a precise loop rate, is
[gripper_teleop_PC_calc.py](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/tree/main/examples/Advanced/SSG48%20gripper%20bilateral%20teleop)
in the Python library's examples, and the [bilateral teleoperation guide](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/guides/bilateral-teleoperation/)
on the STEPFOC site explains the control law with a joint instead of a gripper.
